doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Closing talk about Monk Rowe's name and Clinton
summary: Thanks and goodbyes, joking about the name Monk and Hamilton College's location.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well I’ll tell you this has been a fascinating hour to speak to you.
Well thank you, Monk.
I enjoyed your playing as much as your talking.
The Monk Rowe, I got a Sneed Hern and Monk Rowe. I just love that. Jez what a great name. Where’d you come up with that name? Monk Rowe. Is that your, maybe your folks gave it to you?
No it’s a nickname.
From Thelonious Monk?
Well no actually, from a big blue coat I used to wear.
Oh, like a real monk.
But it is my real name now.
It is.
If you insist on using it, you go right ahead, because I know you will treat it with respect.

Well I’ve been passing myself off as Monk Eastman for years. I don’t know if you ever heard of him. He was an old gangster out of New York. The old, very famous gangster. Dutch Shultz and Monk Eastman were very big rivals.
No kidding. Well on behalf of the college I’d want to thank you for the time.
Well my pleasure.
I hope you have a good gig tonight.
Now what town is this in New York?
Clinton, New York. Hamilton College.
Oh Clinton, New York. From the canal from the steamboat guy.
No, from, yes actually he helped make the Erie Canal and so forth. It’s named after Alexander Hamilton. The college.
Oh, oh, oh, but the town is from the Clinton. So you’ve got a couple of good guys there. Not contemporary, but good. Very good guys, yeah.
All right.
All right, my pleasure.
